risks.note: Management states that despite some correction in cotton prices, the decline in yarn prices was significantly sharper, 'resulting in a wider disparity that adversely affected the margins of yarn spinners across India'. The Company buys a crop and sells a commodity, and the two prices moved apart against it; management adds that 'Volatility in cotton prices continues, with both cotton and yarn prices experiencing wide fluctuations', so the exposure is stated to be live, not resolved.
risks.risk: Cotton-to-yarn spread compression - the core structural risk of a commodity spinner

risks.note: 'Due to geopolitical challenges and sluggish market demand for cotton yarn, spinning mills faced severe pressure on margins. This situation forced many spinning mills across India to operate at lower capacities, with several mills reducing production due to substantial losses in yarn manufacturing.' The Company says its flexible and diversified product range protected its own sales volumes, but the demand backdrop is industry-wide and outside its control.
risks.risk: Weak end-demand for cotton yarn, forcing industry-wide under-utilisation

risks.note: Management identifies 'falling demand for commodity counts' as the thing the value-added strategy must mitigate - yet the value-added leg itself contracted this year: sales volume of Elitwist, Gassing, High Twist, Melange, Core Yarn and Mercerized Yarn 'decreased to 2,800 tonnes during FY 2025-26 from 3,255 tonnes in the previous year'. The stated mitigant weakened in the same period the risk was flagged.
risks.risk: Falling demand specifically for commodity counts, and a value-added mix that shrank in absolute volume

risks.note: 'the Red Sea crisis significantly impacted exports, resulting in higher freight and insurance costs, along with shipping delays.' Exports are a material channel for both yarn (including merchant exports) and fabric, so a shipping-route disruption hits landed cost and lead time simultaneously.

Indian cotton production fell 4% to 313 lakh bales in season 2024-25 on reduced acreage; CAI initially estimated only 305 lakh bales for 2025-26 (arrivals later revised up to 320 lakh bales); CCI procured 91 lakh bales and MSP for medium and long staple cotton was raised 8%, which supports the input price the Company pays. Relief came from a temporary policy action - the Government exempted import duty on cotton only from 30-09-2025 to 31-12-2025 - so the input-cost benefit is time-limited by construction. Looking ahead, USDA FAS data cited by management has global cotton production for 2026-27 declining 5%.
risks.risk: Raw-material availability and policy dependence on the cotton crop

risks.note: Power tariff was increased by Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited and consumption rose, yet power cost fell because own wind farms met 56% of total requirement (PY 50%). Management attributes the improvement to 'better wind velocity, favourable weather conditions' - i.e. a majority of the Company's power economics now rides on weather-dependent generation, and a poor wind year reverses the benefit.
risks.risk: Grid power tariff inflation, mitigated by but also dependent on captive wind

risks.note: Finance cost rose year on year, attributed by management to 'Additional working capital requirements, enhanced Fabric capacity and additional term loan borrowings'. The Company is simultaneously funding modernisation from internal accruals and bank loans while reporting no current tax liability because it is not liable to pay income tax for the year - a combination that makes debt service the binding constraint. (Rupee amounts and leverage ratios deliberately not reproduced here.)
risks.risk: Financing cost and leverage on a loss-making base

risks.note: The only export counterparty named anywhere in the bundle is 'M/s. Asahi Kasei Advance Corporation, Japan', thanked by the Directors 'for their continued support and efforts towards promoting exports to Japan'. The bundle gives no customer-concentration table, so the degree of dependence cannot be quantified - but a single named promoter of a whole export geography is a structural exposure worth tracking.
risks.risk: Customer and channel concentration in exports
